response: ## Accessibility Issue: Hero Image — Missing alternate text (WCAG 1.1.1) **Bug ID:** `A11Y-b4f8c2a1` (instance) / `A11X-f9e3d7b2` (pattern) **URL:** https://news.example.com/articles/spring-garden-guide **XPath:** `//img[@class="hero"]` **Full DOM path:** `/html/body/article[contains(@class, 'feature-story')]/img[@class="hero"]` **WCAG SC:** 1.1.1 Non-text Content (Level A) **Rule:** axe-core 4.9.1 — `image-alt` | ACT Rule: 23a2a8 — Image has non-empty accessible name **Severity:** Critical **Frequency:** 1 instance on this page; cross-site frequency unknown from single scan **Screen type:** desktop | **Colour mode:** light ### HTML Snippet ```html ``` ### Description The hero image within the article feature story lacks an `alt` attribute, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, or `role="presentation"`. Screen reader users will hear only "image" or the raw file path (`hero-2481.jpg`), providing no contextual information about the visual content. This violates WCAG 1.1.1 because the image conveys meaningful context to sighted readers but is completely inaccessible to non-sighted users. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Navigate to https://news.example.com/articles/spring-garden-guide 2. Open a screen reader (e.g., VoiceOver on macOS or NVDA on Windows) 3. Move focus to the hero image at the top of the article body 4. Listen to the screen reader announcement for the image ### Expected Behaviour Screen reader announces a meaningful description of the hero image (e.g., "Spring garden guide: blooming tulips and new seedlings, image"). ### Actual Behaviour Screen reader announces only "image" or reads the file path with no descriptive text. The element has no accessible name. ### Testing Environment | Item | Value | |---|---| | Browser | Chrome 126.0.0.0 | | OS | macOS 14.5 | | Screen reader | N/A (automated scan) | | Testing tool | axe-core 4.9.1 | ### Impact Blind and low-vision users relying on screen readers cannot understand the visual context of the article's hero image. Users who rely on voice control software cannot interact with or describe the image meaningfully. Because this is a critical barrier that blocks comprehension of the page's primary visual content, it requires immediate remediation. ### Suggested Fix (optional) Add a descriptive `alt` attribute if the image conveys information relevant to the article, or add `role="presentation"` and `aria-hidden="true"` if it is purely decorative. ```html ```
